turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry, I'm after running late. The rain coming in from Bray was wicked, and the car park was a pure state.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're grand. Hang on, err, this computer's after freezing again. Right, go on.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I was stuck out there watching some cookery yoke on the telly. Waste of time. I'm wrecked already.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Sorry, say that again? I was clicking through a pile of results.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): The telly was useless. Can we get on with it, I've no patience left today.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Of course. What's brought you in?

[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Pain up under the ribs on the right, after anything fatty, a fry or cheese. A bout lasts three or four hours, and it's been a couple of months. Well, maybe six weeks. No, a couple of months.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right side after fatty food. Did you vomit with it at all?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Once. Umm, last week, after a takeaway. Brought the whole dinner back up, and the pain still went on.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever with these turns?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it shoot through to the back, or up into the shoulder?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. What are you taking when it starts? And the length of a bout, say it again, I half heard.
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Three or four hours, I told you. Gaviscon, ten mils, when it comes on. Takes the edge off, not by much.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your regular tablets now. The list on screen is half blank. Run through them slowly.

[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Amlodipine for the pressure, 5 milligrams in the morning. The cholesterol one at night, twenty milligrams, I can never remember the name of it. Sugar tablets, metformin, 500 milligrams in the morning. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, a teaspoon, from the health shop.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cholesterol one, the dose again, the cursor jumped.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Twenty milligrams at night. It's a white tablet. I don't know the name.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): God, the weather. I was meant to bring the grandson to the playground and it lashed rain. He's 6, mad into the hurling, won't sit still.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hurling, is it. My nephew's the same with the football, never in the house. Where were we, it ate a line.
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Hurling, not football. Completely different. I'm not here about him.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has anyone belonging to you had the gallbladder out? I'm asking because of the pain after greasy meals.
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): My mother, yeah. She had the gallbladder surgery, years ago. They said it was the same sort of pain.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking this could be the gallbladder, biliary colic. Can't say for certain until we have a look.
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that serious? She was in bits with hers, I remember that much.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't leap to surgery talk. We need the picture first. Sorry, your mother, say that bit again?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Gallbladder surgery. Years back. I already said it.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, got it that time.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): So what are you doing about it. I can't keep missing work.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll book blood tests, the liver ones as well, and an ultrasound of the tummy. Reception'll have the forms, both of them arranged.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks for the results. Lay off the fry-ups till then, they set it off.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Two weeks, fine. I'll try. I'm too tired to argue about the chips.

spec.situation: Woman with right-upper stomach pain after fatty meals, lasting hours, once with vomiting; takes antacid; mother had gallbladder surgery; blood tests and ultrasound planned.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Pain, duration, fatty trigger, 3-4 hour bouts, Gaviscon supported; body site stated as under right ribs, not explicitly right upper abdomen.
bad.text: Right upper abdominal pain (category=gastrointestinal, status=present, duration=approximately 2 months, frequency=bouts lasting 3 to 4 hours after fatty meals, temporality=current, body_site=right upper abdomen, aggravating_factors=fatty meals, relieving_factors=Gaviscon, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Past medical history of diabetes mellitus ('sugar'; on metformin) is stated but not recorded in past medical history.
Gaviscon only 'takes the edge off, not by much' for the pain; limited relief not recorded.
Possible radiation of the pain to the back or shoulder was asked and answered equivocally ('Sometimes, not really'); this uncertainty is not recorded.
